name: Cloud Tasks
oneLiner: Managed task queue for decoupling and dispatching asynchronous work.
whatItIs: Cloud Tasks is Google Cloud's managed queue for dispatching asynchronous work to worker services. A producer enqueues a task — typically an HTTP request to be delivered later — and Cloud Tasks reliably dispatches it to a handler (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, App Engine or any endpoint), with rate limiting, retries and scheduling. Its focus is explicit task execution and flow control: you decide how fast tasks are delivered and how failures retry. Where Pub/Sub is a streaming messaging bus for events fanned out to many subscribers, Cloud Tasks is about handing off individual units of work to be executed, decoupling the producer from slower back-end processing.

inPractice.narrative: A web request needs to kick off a slow job (say, generating a report) without making the user wait. The app enqueues a Cloud Task pointing at a worker endpoint and returns immediately. Cloud Tasks dispatches the task to the worker at a controlled rate, retrying on failure with backoff, so a burst of requests doesn't overwhelm the back end. It's the buffer that decouples the fast front end from slower asynchronous processing, with explicit control over dispatch rate.

coreConcepts.detail: Tasks are usually HTTP requests Cloud Tasks delivers to a worker endpoint (Cloud Run/Functions/App Engine/any URL) — explicit hand-off of a unit of work.
Per-queue controls on dispatch rate and max concurrent tasks protect back-ends from overload — a defining feature versus a raw stream.
Configurable retry policies with exponential backoff make task execution reliable without custom retry code.
Tasks can be scheduled for future delivery, enabling deferred/delayed work (e.g. run this in 10 minutes).
Unlike Pub/Sub's publish-and-subscribe, the producer names the target and controls execution — task-oriented rather than event-broadcast.
Cloud Tasks = dispatch individual tasks with flow control; Pub/Sub = high-throughput event messaging fanned out to many subscribers. Different jobs.

whenToUse: Offloading slow work from a request path to async workers.
Controlling dispatch rate/concurrency to protect back-end services.
Reliable, retryable task execution with backoff.
Explicit hand-off of individual tasks to named endpoints.
whenNotToUse: High-throughput event streaming to many subscribers — use Pub/Sub.
Replayable event logs / analytics streams — use Pub/Sub or managed Kafka.
Simple in-process background work with no reliability needs.
Fan-out broadcast patterns — Pub/Sub fits better.

keyFacts.label: Targets
keyFacts.value: HTTP endpoints — Cloud Run, Functions, App Engine, any URL.

keyFacts.label: Flow control
keyFacts.value: Per-queue rate limiting and concurrency caps.

keyFacts.label: Reliability
keyFacts.value: Configurable retries with backoff; scheduled delivery.

keyFacts.label: Contrast
keyFacts.value: Task dispatch vs Pub/Sub event streaming.

keyFacts.label: Billing
keyFacts.value: Per task operation (with a free monthly tier).

pricingShape: Cloud Tasks bills per operation (roughly, per task dispatched) with a free monthly allotment, and nothing to provision — cost scales with task volume, and idle queues cost nothing. The worker services that execute tasks (Cloud Run/Functions) are billed separately for their own compute. The main lever is simply task volume; the flow-control features that make it valuable (rate limiting, retries) don't add a separate charge. It's an inexpensive way to add reliable, controlled async execution to an app.
gotchas: It dispatches tasks, it doesn't stream events — for fan-out/streaming use Pub/Sub instead.
The worker endpoint must be idempotent — retries can deliver a task more than once.
Rate-limit and concurrency settings must match the worker's capacity, or you either throttle or overload it.
Very high fan-out broadcast is the wrong shape for Cloud Tasks — that's Pub/Sub's job.
Worker compute (Cloud Run/Functions) is a separate cost from the queue — budget both.

equivalents.name: Amazon SQS
equivalents.note: Managed work queue; consumers poll rather than Cloud Tasks pushing to endpoints.

equivalents.note: Enterprise broker with queues + topics and richer messaging features.
